subject: Request: Exclude customer-managed maintenance from Private SLA uptime
messages:
From: Priya Shah <priya@northshorehealth.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
Cc: DevOps Team <devops@northshorehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Exclude customer-managed maintenance from Private SLA uptime

Hi Avery,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. We're getting close to the on-prem rollout and have one ask before we sign: our platform team will require regular maintenance windows and occasional emergency firewall updates that are customer-initiated. During those events we anticipate short bursts (typically 3–15 minutes) of packet loss or increased latency.

Can Redwood exclude customer-controlled maintenance (scheduled maintenance windows and emergency customer-side network changes) from the Private/VPC SLA uptime and latency calculations? We need this carved out in the contract and a short, objective definition so our procurement/legal can approve.

I've attached our maintenance calendar for Q3 and a trimmed network trace showing the patterns. Happy to hop on a call to walk through specifics.

Thanks,
Priya Shah
Head of Cloud Platform
Northshore Health
Attachments: maintenance_calendar.csv (2 KB), sample_network_trace.pcap (400 KB)
From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Shah <priya@northshorehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Exclude customer-managed maintenance from Private SLA uptime

Hi Priya —

Appreciate the clear examples and the traces. Short answer: yes, we can define a shared-responsibility exception for customer-controlled network events, but we need to be explicit about the operational signals and evidence required so we don't unintentionally create a broad carve-out.

Could you confirm two things for us:
- Scheduled maintenance windows defined at least 48 hours in advance (as UTC time ranges) that your team publishes to a shared calendar.
- Emergency changes: an on-call ticket reference + firewall change ticket showing time window and rollback action.

I'll loop in our ops and legal folks with a proposed clause. If that works, I'll send a short draft for signature (DocuSign).

Two quick notes from our side: when customer-side actions impact request latency but the request still reached our nodes, we may still record higher server-side processing times; the SLA exclusion would apply only to availability/edge-network attribution, not to Redwood runtime errors. We'll detail this in the clause.

Best,
Avery Johnson
Account Executive — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 17 Aug 2027 08:23:00 -0700
Subject: FW: Request: Exclude customer-managed maintenance from Private SLA uptime

Team — forwarding Northshore's ask. They want an explicit SLA carve-out for customer-controlled maintenance windows and emergency firewall changes. Quick asks:

- Soojin: please propose the operational definition and telemetry signals we should require (logs/trace evidence, DRG entries, HA failover markers).
- Naomi: any compliance/security concerns if we accept a carve-out that references customer-supplied ticket evidence?
- Karthik: this is mid-stage in procurement (DEAL-78912). What's the minimum contractual language Sales should be comfortable with?

Goal is to keep the exception narrow, objective, and evidence-based. I think we can propose a standard paragraph + an optional appendix with customer-supplied maintenance schedule.

Thanks —
Avery
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 17 Aug 2027 10:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FW: Request: Exclude customer-managed maintenance from Private SLA uptime

Avery / Karthik —

Suggested operational definition (draft):
"""
Customer-Controlled Network Events: scheduled maintenance windows (published minimum 48 hours in advance) and emergency customer-side network changes initiated by the customer's authorized contacts that directly impact connectivity between Customer-managed edge infrastructure and Redwood's ingress points. For an event to be eligible for SLA exclusion, Customer must provide: (a) a published maintenance window or ticket with timestamps, (b) network trace (pcap or equivalent) or aggregated flow logs demonstrating packet loss/latency during the window, and (c) confirmation of rollback or remediation within 24 hours for emergency changes.
"""

Telemetry/evidence we should accept: aggregated flow logs (NetFlow/sFlow), packet captures with timestamps, firewall change ticket IDs, and calendar invite IDs. For emergency events, acceptance requires a ticket with a sequence of events (change -> observed impact -> remediation).

Operational fallback: We recommend a contractual requirement for a secondary routing policy: if customer-provided network health is degraded for >5 minutes and we detect request failures exceeding 5% over a 1-minute window, Redwood will (i) attempt failover to an alternate path if configured, and (ii) offer a hosted fallback for critical routes if the customer opts into that feature (charged as separate service).

Naomi: please flag any red-lines.

— Soojin
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Shah <priya@northshorehealth.com>, Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
Cc: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 20 Aug 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Exclude customer-managed maintenance from Private SLA uptime

Hi Priya / Avery —

Thanks — we've reviewed the proposed language and are comfortable with an evidence-based carve-out with these guardrails:
- Evidence must be machine-verifiable (logs/traces/ticket metadata) and retained for 90 days.
- Exceptions are permissive only for network/connectivity attribution; Redwood runtime errors (process crashes, OOMs, model-serving errors) remain in scope.
- For emergency changes, customer must designate an authorized contact list in writing; undocumented ad-hoc changes are not eligible.

Priya: we'll prepare a short appendix and a redlined paragraph for the SOW. Avery will send the DocuSign when ready. If Northshore needs faster processing, please provide a sample ticket and calendar entry so we can validate the evidence format.

Naomi Feldman
Director, Security & Trust
Redwood Inference
